summary: Spike of throttles during cross-region embedding backfill after enabling per-route burst isolation
description:
Issue summary: Customer started a large cross-region embedding backfill (US->EU) after switching to a per-route burst-isolation policy. Within 20 minutes they began seeing sustained 429 responses across many short-lived streaming upload sessions.

Impact: Backfill stalled, client resumed with aggressive retries and experienced token exhaustion for other application routes. Customer reported user-facing delays for embedding lookups. Estimated affected requests: ~1.2M over the first hour.

Environment: Redwood hosted (dedicated pool) serving-runtime behind edge proxies; customer using ephemeral API keys created by their ingestion workers. Regions: us-west primary clients, eu-west target storage/replication.

Observed behaviour: Rapid 429s with inconsistent rate-limit headers (Retry-After fluctuating between 1-5s, X-RateLimit-Remaining reported 0 then non-zero mid-session). 429s appear correlated with bursts of new short streaming sessions (multipart chunk uploads) rather than sustained token throughput.

Expected behaviour: Per-route burst isolation should prevent short-lived upload bursts from draining tenant-level sustained quota; customers should see clear throttle headers and no cross-route leakage.

Priority rationale: Customer dedicated environment; production backlog blocked; affecting model embeddings used in search ranking for calls to live traffic.
steps_to_reproduce: Enable per-route burst isolation on a dedicated pool tenant
Launch ~400 parallel short-lived streaming upload sessions that each stream ~50-200 tokens then close (simulate multipart chunked backfill)
Observe 2xx success initially, then escalate to 429 responses across multiple routes within ~10-30 minutes
Capture response headers and client retry patterns
logs:
Sample throttle response headers captured at 2026-03-12T15:28:14Z:
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Limit: 600000
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 163
Retry-After: 2
X-Route-Id: upload-chunk-route-42

Client trace shows immediate retry after 2s and next request also 429. Datadog span links: https://dd.example.com/dashboards/embeddings-backfill-uploads (customer-facing link shared in thread).
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: client-side retry fan-out is amplifying short window burst accounting and causing tenant depletion
Found edge-proxy pooled IP accounting inconsistent with per-route isolation; health-check pings from origin were being attributed to the same route counter in some edge regions
Observed mismatch between route-layer counters and tenant-layer token buckets during rollup window (route counters show >100% of tenant allowance during micro windows)
Reproduced locally with a reduced worker set and saw the same rapid exhaustion pattern when session churn rate increased beyond ~300 sessions/min
Config audit: customer's per-route burst isolation was enabled concurrently with a reduced tenant token window (small delta) — combination likely exacerbated double-counting in short windows
comments: 2026-03-12 15:45 - Support (Aisha Patel): Acknowledged, collecting logs and asked customer to pause the backfill. Requested trace IDs and primary worker hostnames.
2026-03-12 16:10 - Customer (Emily Chen, LexiSearch): Paused ingestion; provided worker hostnames x3 and sample trace IDs trace-7a2, trace-7a3.

2026-03-12 17:02 - SRE (Liam O'Connor): Identified edge-proxy health-check attribution bug in eu-west region that increments route counters for ephemeral sessions. Raised INT-45821 for internal follow-up and hotfix.

2026-03-13 09:20 - Support (Aisha Patel): Temporary mitigation applied: excluded health-check IP range from rate accounting for the affected edge fleet and increased per-route burst allowance for LexiSearch tenant. Customer resumed backfill at reduced parallelism.

2026-03-14 11:05 - SRE (Liam O'Connor): Deploying patch to rate-limiter to ensure route->tenant aggregation dedupes health-check increments during micro-windows. Monitoring will run for 24h post-deploy.
resolution: Workaround applied: health-check IP range excluded from rate accounting and per-route burst allowance temporarily increased for the tenant. Customer resumed at lower concurrency while SRE deployed a patch. Patch ensures health-checks are not double-counted in route->tenant aggregation. Post-deploy monitoring show error rate back to baseline. Follow-up: change default per-route burst window to be more conservative and add a CI test to exercise high session churn.
